about: Bars of a measured grid, shows/scenes/deadmau5 - Strobe (Special Features Remix).beats: bar b starts at 0.136 + 1.875 b seconds (128.000 BPM), 210 bars, flat to 5 ms. The bar line is where the phrases turn, every 8 bars from bar 0, and every hole in the bass (71.5, 79, 87, 95, 151.5, 159, 167, 175) is on it. THE CINEMA. A remix called Special Features gets a film, and the song runs through the history of cinema. The ears are the projector's two reels, turning clockwise as reels do; their rims are the sprocket holes, and the tick that opens the track is the film going through the gate. The lamp warms, then the leader counts eight to one, a turn of the clock hand a bar. The picture starts in silver with grain, a scratch and a film strip running along the jaw, and the title crosses once. Then the first film there was: a galloping horse. The kick brings the only character, a very small mau5 walking across the silent screen in sepia. A clapper slams on the one hit at 48, the iris closes, and there is almost nothing but dust until searchlights swing up from the bottom of the dome for a premiere, still in black and white. The first drop goes to Technicolor, and nothing before it has had a colour in it. Red velvet parts on a moving dye picture; reel two is a Busby Berkeley kaleidoscope, reel three premiere night with marquee bulbs round the dome, reel four the three colour strips sliding in and out of register. Every hole in the bass is a reel change: black screen, holes racing, the cue mark blinking top right as it does in a real print, and the next reel spinning up on the other ear. The second breakdown is a flashback in silver, the mau5 alone. The rolling bass is the train arriving, as in 1896, and it takes him with it. The groove is hand-tinted silent film: a kick line of three mau5s in amber, then the moon in night blue with a rocket on its way to its eye, which lands exactly as the riser starts. In the long riser the film jumps its sprockets: the frame line rolls faster and faster, the lamp gets hotter, and the leader comes back to count three, two, one. A second clap, the one white moment, alone on a black dome, then the mau5 himself in colour with no more curtains; the kick line comes back gold over the kaleidoscope and the moon watches the second premiere. The only real strobe in the show is on the ears alone, in the dark, on the last riser, bar 175. Then the colour drains away, he walks off down the road getting smaller as an iris follows him, the film jams on a blank frame and burns out from the middle on the final riser. The ear flashes are kept where the power guard leaves the shell lit: over 1000 mA it sheds the shell at s^6, so each reel steps aside for the two beats of its hit, and the backgrounds are low so the characters have the shell's 300 mA to themselves. Nothing on the shell pulses faster than an 8th note.
